assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines Katori's magic-wavelength idea with Ye's demonstration of record accuracy and stability, and is the leading route to redefining the second. It is a direct realization of pushing what we can measure and how accurately, with downstream use in tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and searches for new physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed magic-wavelength trapping and made the early strontium demonstrations; Ye's group drove the precision, coherence and systematics frontier. The two-name configuration is clean, though other groups (for example in Paris, Boulder and Germany) contributed to the maturation and this list does not credit them.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of independent confirmation from several national laboratories, with agreement at the 10^-18 level; the technology is mature and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to pair clocks with another precision-measurement topic or with the frequency-comb prize already given in 2005 is unclear.
Exact priority among early lattice-clock proposals is from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices turned the Hubbard model into a controllable laboratory system and opened a general platform for many-body physics. The Mott-insulator transition, single-site imaging and later work on dynamics and topology have had broad impact across atomic and condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with collaborators in the original proposal) supplied the theoretical blueprint; Greiner and Bloch carried out the decisive Mott-insulator experiments and the development of quantum-gas microscopes. Hansch/Kasevich-type contributions and the roles of Cirac and others are not supplied in this list, and Cirac overlaps with other candidates, so the three-name split is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely reproduced by many independent groups; the field is mature, and the quantum-gas microscope era is well established.
uncertainties: Whether the prize is best framed as the lattice platform or as quantum simulation in general.
Overlap of Zoller and Cirac with other atomic-physics candidates may constrain how many such prizes are plausible.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal showed how laser-cooled trapped ions could host quantum gates, and experimental work then realized high-fidelity entangling gates, teleportation and small algorithms. It is a foundational demonstration that a physical system can serve as a programmable quantum processor.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the theoretical proposal; Blatt led key experimental realizations of ion-trap gates and entanglement. Wineland, whose group is central to the experimental history and who shared the 2012 prize, is not in the credited names, which complicates a fair attribution of the experimental side.
assessment.maturity: Strong, independent confirmation across several groups and a mature commercial and academic ecosystem; recognition is timely, although the 2012 prize partly covered the experimental ground.
uncertainties: How much of the field's credit is already addressed by the 2012 prize.
Whether the near-duplicate atomic quantum information candidate (B035) would be treated as the same discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics established strong coupling of a superconducting qubit to a microwave resonator, which became the architecture for readout, coupling and control of superconducting quantum processors. Its importance for quantum technology is high and the concepts are cleanly rooted in cavity QED.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf published the 2004 proposal and the first strong-coupling demonstrations; Girvin is not in the supplied credited names. Among the supplied names, Schoelkopf and Wallraff are decisive experimentally and Blais theoretically.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and independently confirmed; recognition could be seen as timely, but a recent prize on macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits may reduce room for a second circuit prize soon.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recent superconducting-circuit recognition and the omission of Girvin from the credited names.
Exact precedence between cQED and earlier circuit-QED proposals is not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical addressing and coherent control of single spins in diamond and other solid-state hosts opened a room-temperature platform for quantum sensing, quantum memories and networks. It matches the theme that measurement capability limits science, and it has been very productive for nanoscale magnetometry and biological sensing.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's group reported optical detection of single NV centres and coherent control early on; Awschalom contributed broadly to spin coherence in semiconductors and defects. Lukin and Walsworth have major contributions in sensing and quantum control, so the two-name choice is only one fair option and the allocation is genuinely uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many groups with a large body of applications; commercial and quantum-network applications are growing, so recognition is reasonably timely though still evolving.
uncertainties: Genuinely unclear which three of four credited people best capture the decisive contributions.
The candidate is a compound field of several systems (NV, SiC, rare-earth hosts), which may need different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programmable arrays of individually trapped Rydberg atoms combine tweezers, blockade interactions and rearrangement to realize quantum simulation and computation with hundreds of qubits. Scientific impact is high and growing rapidly, with tests of many-body physics and error-corrected logical operations.
assessment.attribution: Saffman and collaborators proposed Rydberg-blockade gates; Browaeys and Lukin led experimental demonstrations of programmable many-body arrays. Zoller contributed key early proposals and is credited but is a lower priority here given overlaps with other candidates.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing with several independent groups, but conclusions about computational advantage and error correction are still developing, so recognition may be slightly early.
uncertainties: The pace of the field may change who is seen as decisive in a few years.
Zoller's role and overlap with other candidates affect the best three-person configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cooling and controlling molecules at ultracold temperatures enables precision tests (such as the electron electric dipole moment), controlled chemistry and new quantum-simulation platforms. The importance is clear and the connection to precision measurement is strong.
assessment.attribution: DeMille, Doyle and Ye each made distinct contributions (buffer-gas cooling, laser cooling of molecules, ACME-type electron EDM measurements and cold-molecule quantum control). The allocation to three is plausible but the decisive discovery is somewhat diffuse, and Ye also features on another candidate.
assessment.maturity: Experimental methods are now confirmed by several groups, but the most compelling scientific payoffs (EDM bounds beyond the standard model, controlled chemistry) are still emerging, so it is somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Diffuse discovery definition across cooling methods and applications.
Whether a single prize can fairly cover both molecular cooling and EDM precision tests.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution links quantum foundations with practical security and has driven a worldwide experimental and commercial program. The BB84 protocol and Ekert's entanglement-based protocol are conceptually original and have lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard's 1984 protocol and Ekert's 1991 protocol are the decisive conceptual contributions. Jian-Wei Pan's role is the experimental and satellite demonstration, which is a different type of achievement and would complicate a three-person limit; I leave him out in this proposal.
assessment.maturity: Conceptually mature and experimentally demonstrated over fibre and satellite links, but practical security loopholes and deployment remain open and the 2022 prize already recognized related entanglement work.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on entanglement and quantum information.
Whether the prize would favour theory or the experimental networks, which splits credit.
